A series is given, with one number missing. Choose the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

questions.question: In a certain code language, '+' represents '×', '-' represents '+', '×' represents '÷' and '÷' represents '-'. What is the answer to the following question? 42 × 7 ÷ 7 + 9 - 62 = ?
questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language, '+' represents '×', '-' represents '+', '×' represents '÷' and '÷' represents '-'. What is the answer to the following question?

42 × 7 ÷ 7 + 9 - 62 = ?
questions.solution:
Converting the given equation according to the code language:

42 × 7 ÷ 7 + 9 – 62 = 42 ÷ 7 – 7 × 9 + 62 = 6 – 63 + 62 = 5

questions.question: Chirag's birthday is on Thursday 1 st June. On what day of the week will be Reyansh's Birthday in the same year if Reyansh was born on 3 rd December?
questions.questionHtml: Chirag's birthday is on Thursday 1<sup>st</sup> June. On what day of the week will be Reyansh's Birthday in the same year if Reyansh was born on 3<sup>rd</sup> December?
questions.solution:
Total number of days from 1st June to 1st December = 30 + 31 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 = 183

When we divide 183 by 7 we get remainder 1, that means 1st December is Friday. (As the quotient is 21 in this case, means there are 21 weeks from 1st June and 30th November and it further implies 30th November is Thursday.)

Hence, 2nd December is Saturday and 3rd December is Sunday.

questions.question: If 17@1 = 8; 9@1 = 4; 6@4 = 1; then what is the value of 8@2 = ?
questions.questionHtml: If 17@1 = 8; 9@1 = 4; 6@4 = 1; then what is the value of <u>8@2</u> = ?
questions.solution:
17@1 = (17 – 1) ÷ 2 = 16 ÷ 2 = 8

9@1 = (9 – 1) ÷ 2 = 8 ÷ 2 = 4

6@4 = (6 – 4) ÷ 2 = 2 ÷ 2 = 1

Similarly,

8@2 = (8 – 2) ÷ 2 = 6 ÷ 2 = 3

questions.question: The weights of 4 boxes are 20, 40, 50 and 30 kilograms. Which of the following cannot be the total weight, in kilograms, of any combination of these boxes and in a combination a box can be used only once?
questions.questionHtml: The weights of 4 boxes are 20, 40, 50 and 30 kilograms. Which of the following cannot be the total weight, in kilograms, of any combination of these boxes and in a combination a box can be used only once?
questions.solution:
Sum of weight of all the boxes = 20 + 40 + 50 + 30 = 140 kg

Sum of weight of two boxes having weight of 40kg and 50 kg = 40 + 50 = 90 kg

Sum of weight of three boxes having weight 40 kg, 50 kg and 30 kg = 40 + 50 + 30 = 120 kg

As we have found the possibility of three weights, hence by elimination method we can say that 130 kg weight is not possible from the given weights.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Right in the Indian Constitution allows citizens to move the court if they believe that any of their Fundamental Rights have been violated by the State?
questions.questionHtml: Which Fundamental Right in the Indian Constitution allows citizens to move the court if they believe that any of their Fundamental Rights have been violated by the State?
questions.solution:
• Article 32 provides the right to Constitutional remedies which means that a person has the right to move to Supreme Court (and high courts also) for getting his fundamental rights protected.
  • While Supreme Court has the power to issue writs under article 32, High Courts have been given the same powers under article 226.
  • Further, the power to issue writs can also be extended to any other courts (including local courts) by Parliament via making a law for local limits of the jurisdiction of such courts.

Additional Information 

  • It is called the “soul of the constitution and very heart of it” by Dr. Ambedkar.
  • Supreme Court has included it in basic structure doctrine.
  • Further, it is made clear that right to move to Supreme Court cannot be suspended except otherwise provided by the Constitution. This implies that this right suspended during a national emergency under article 352.​

questions.question: In science, a push or pull of an object is called ________.
questions.questionHtml: In science, a push or pull of an object is called ________.
questions.solution:
CONCEPT:

  • Force: A force is a push or pull acting upon an object as a result of its interaction with another object.
  • A force acting for a given amount of time will change an object's momentum ( or say velocity if the mass is being constant).
  • Velocity is the rate of change of position with respect to time, whereas acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
  • Forces cause acceleration in the body.

​EXPLANATION:

  • A force can cause an object with mass to change its velocity (which includes ​beginning moving from a state of rest), i.e., to accelerate.
  • Force can also be described intuitively as a push or a pull.

So option 3 is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers flows from India to Pakistan?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following rivers flows from India to Pakistan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e Satluj

There are five rivers that flow from India into Pakistan: Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Satluj.​

Sutlej River, Ancient Greek Zaradros, Sanskrit Shutudri, or Shatadru, longest of the five tributaries of the Indus River that give Punjab (meaning “Five Rivers”) its name.

It rises on the north slope of the Himalayas in Lake La’nga in southwestern Tibet, at an elevation above 15,000 feet (4,600 meters). Flowing northwestward and then west-southwestward through Himalayan gorges, it enters and crosses the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh before beginning its flow through the Punjab plain near Nangal, Punjab state.

It receives the Beas River and forms 65 miles (105 km) of the India-Pakistan border before entering Pakistan and flowing another 220 miles (350 km) to join the Chenab River west of Bahawalpur.

questions.question: Which of the following mountain ranges do the Patkai hills belong to?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following mountain ranges do the Patkai hills belong to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Purvanchal.

Key Points

  • The Purvanchal range includes the mountain ranges of the Patkai hills, the Barail range, Manipur, and Naga Hills.
  • Purvachal, also called the Eastern Highlands, mountain range in eastern India. They extend over an area of about 37,900 square miles (98,000 square km) in Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, and eastern Assam states. 
  • The area is bounded by Bangladesh to the southwest, Myanmar (Burma) to the southeast, and China to the northeast. The Hindu epic the Mahabharata has several references to the region.
  • Purvanchal range bends sharply to the south beyond the Dihang River gorge and spreads along the eastern boundary of India with Myanmar.
  • The Purvachal was ruled by the Ahoms from the beginning of the 13th century. It was occupied by the British in the last quarter of the 19th century.

questions.question: Jama Masjid of Delhi was built by?
questions.questionHtml: Jama Masjid of Delhi was built by?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Shah Jahan.

Key Points

  • The period of Shah Jahan’s reign is widely considered to be the golden age of Mughal architecture. He commissioned many monuments and they are:
  • Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Jama Masjid (Agra and Delhi), Moti Masjid (Agra Fort).
  • Jama Masjid was built between 1644 and 1656.
  • Shah Jahan was the 5th Mughal Emperor.

Additional Information

Jama Masjid (Agra)

  • Jama Masjid is located just opposite the Agra fort.
  • It was dedicated to his daughter, Jahanara Begum.
  • Jama Masjid is also known as the 'Friday mosques'.
  • Jama Masjid is one of the largest mosques in India.
  • The Jama Masjid is built mainly of red sandstone and marble that stand as a testimony to the magnificent Mughal architecture.
  • It has a fountain at the centre and is supported by four kiosks in the courtyard.
  • The interior walls have scriptures in the Persian style praising Shah Jahan and Jahan Ara.
  • The inlaid panels of work here are quite similar to that of the Taj Mahal and are common to all the monuments and structures built by the Mughals in Agra.
  • The Tomb of Salim Chisti is a part of the mosque compound.

Red Fort

  • Red Fort is located in Old Delhi was built by Shah Jahan in 1638.
  • Red Fort is also known as Lal Qila.
  • The Red sandstone walls of the massive Red Fort rise 33-m above the clamour of Old Delhi as a reminder of the magnificent power and pomp of the Mughal emperors.
  • Lahori Gate is the main entrance to the Red Fort.
  • Shah Jahan Shifted the capital from Agra to Delhi.

Agra Fort

  • Agra Fort is located in Agra.
  • The construction of the Agra fort was started around 1565, when the initial structures were built by the Mughal Emperor Akbar, and subsequently taken over by his grandson Shah Jahan, who added most of the marble creations to the fort. 
  • It was the main residence of the emperors of the Mughal Dynasty till 1638 when the capital was shifted from Agra to Delhi.
  • The Agra Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

​Important Points

Jama Masjid with gateway Buland Darwaza Fatehpur Sikri

Part of work done by A in 1 day = 1/12

Part of work done by B in 1 day = 1/8

And part of work done by C in 1 day = 1/24

When they work together, part of work finished by all three in one day \(= \frac{1}{{12}} + \frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{{24}}\)

Let’s assume that they together can finish the entire work in x days

\(x\left( {\frac{1}{{12}} + \frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{{24}}} \right) = 1\)

⇒ x ((2 + 3 + 1)/24) = 1

⇒ 6x/24 = 1

⇒ x = 4

∴ Together they’ll finish the work in 4 days

questions.question: If a 3 + b 3 = 19 and a + b = 1, then what is the value of ab?

It is given that a3 + b3 = 19 and a + b = 1

Then,

13 = 19 + 3ab(1)

⇒ 3ab = -18

⇒ ab = -6

Assume, a = 3 and b = -2

These values satisfied both the given conditions

questions.question: Point P is the midpoint of segment AB. Co-ordinates of P are (3, 1) and B are (5, -4). What are the co-ordinates of point A?

questions.question: If in 2 years at simple interest the principal increases by 18%, what will be the compound interest (in Rs) earned on Rs. 7000 in 3 years at the same rate?
questions.questionHtml: If in 2 years at simple interest the principal increases by 18%, what will be the compound interest (in Rs) earned on Rs. 7000 in 3 years at the same rate?
questions.solution:
let principal amount at simple interest be 100

a/q the amount become 118 in 2 years at simple interest

⇒ Simple interest = 118 - 100 = 18

So, SI = P × R × T/100

⇒ 18 = 100 × R × 2/100

⇒ R = 9%

Therefore,

\(\begin{array}{l} CI = P{\left( {1 + \frac{9}{{100}}} \right)^3} - P\\ \Rightarrow \;CI = 7000{\left( {1 + \frac{9}{{100}}} \right)^3} - 7000 \end{array}\)

⇒ CI = 7000 × 109/100 × 109/100 × 109/100 - 7000

∴ Compound interest = Rs. 2065.20

questions.question: The average weight of P, Q and R is 45 kg. If the average weight of P and Q be 36.5 kg and that of Q and R be 52 kg, then what is the weight (in kgs) of Q?
questions.questionHtml: The average weight of P, Q and R is 45 kg. If the average weight of P and Q be 36.5 kg and that of Q and R be 52 kg, then what is the weight (in kgs) of Q?
questions.solution:
Average weight of P, Q and R = 45 kg

Total weight of all together = P + Q + R = 45 × 3 = 135      ----(i)

Average weight of P and Q be 36.5 and Q and R be 52 kg

P + Q = 36.5 × 2 = 73      ----(ii)

Q + R = 52 × 2 = 104       ----(iii)

On solving eq. (i) and (ii)

Weight of R = 62

Then from eq. (iii)

⇒ Q + 62 = 104

⇒ Q = 42

∴ Weight of Q is 42 kg

questions.question: If x/3 - [5/2(7x/5 - 4/3)] = -x/6, then what is the value of x?
questions.questionHtml: If x/3 - [5/2(7x/5 - 4/3)] = -x/6, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
\(\begin{array}{l} \frac{x}{3} - \left[ {\frac{5}{2}\left( {\frac{{7x}}{5} - \frac{4}{3}} \right)} \right] = \frac{{ - x}}{6}\\ \Rightarrow \frac{x}{3} + \frac{x}{6} = \left[ {\frac{5}{2}\left( {\frac{{7x}}{5} - \frac{4}{3}} \right)} \right]\\ \Rightarrow \frac{{2x\; + \;x}}{6} = \left[ {\frac{5}{2}\left( {\frac{{21x - 20}}{{15}}} \right)} \right] \end{array}\)

⇒ 3x = 21x - 20

⇒ x = 10/9

questions.question: What is the reflection of the point (-2, 5) in the line x = -1?
questions.questionHtml: What is the reflection of the point (-2, 5) in the line x = -1?
questions.solution:
When a point is reflected about the y-axis, the y-coordinate remains the same and only the x-coordinate is transformed

∵ The line x = -1 is parallel to the y-axis, y-coordinate will remain the same after reflection

Now, along the x-direction, the distance between the reflected point and the line will be equal to the distance between the original point and the line

⇒ Distance between point and line along x-direction = ।-1 - (-2)। = ।1। = 1 unit

⇒ X-coordinate of reflection = -1 + 1 = 0

∴ The reflection point is (0, 5)

questions.question: A fraction is greater than its reciprocal by 72/77. What is the fraction?
questions.questionHtml: A fraction is greater than its reciprocal by 72/77. What is the fraction?
questions.solution:
One thing is clear that fraction must be greater than it’s reciprocal

Now going through the option, we can easily eliminate option 1st and 3rd because its reciprocal is greater than the respective fractions

∴ Option 4th by solving

Alternative solution:

Let the friction be x

So, x - 1/x = 72/77

⇒ (x2 - 1) /x = 72/77

⇒ 77x2 - 72x - 77 =0

⇒ x = 11/7 and (-7)/11

∴ Friction = 11/7

Let say number = x/y

then reciprocal = y/x

⇒ x/y - y/x = 72/77

⇒ x2 – y2 = 72xy/77

⇒ 77x2 – 77y2 – 72xy = 0

⇒ 77x2 – 72xy – 77y2 = 0

⇒ 77x2 – 121xy + 49xy – 77y2 = 0

⇒ 11x(7x – 11y) + 7y(7x – 11y) = 0

⇒ (11x + 7y) (7x - 11y) =0

x/y = -7/11  or  11/7

questions.question: If Tan θ = 7/24, then what is the value of Sec θ?

questions.solution:

Hypotenuse2 (h) = perpendicular2(p) + base2(b)

⇒ Hypotenuse2 (h) = 25

∴ Sec θ = (hypotenuse(h)) / (base(b)) = 25/24

'Veneration' means 'great respect for something'. On the other hand, 'contempt' means 'disrespect or disregard for something'.

Hence, the two words have opposite meanings.

The other words, 'adoration', 'admiration' and 'reverence' are synonymous with 'veneration'.

questions.question: In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. The diamond necklace was _______ too extravagant for a simple dinner party.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.

The diamond necklace was _______ too extravagant for a simple dinner party.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 4' i.e. 'Far'.

Key Points

  • The correct answer is "far".
  • In this context, the adjective "far" is used to indicate a high degree of something, and it's usually paired with another adjective.
  • So, the phrase "far too extravagant" means that the diamond necklace is excessively or extremely extravagant.

Therefore, the sentence would read: "The diamond necklace was far too extravagant for a simple dinner party." 

Additional Information

  • Here is why the other options are incorrect:
    • "Distance" is a noun that refers to the amount of space between two points, and it does not fit in this context.
    • "Long" is typically used to describe length or duration, not the degree of extravagance.
    • "Very much" is typically used with verbs or as a response to a question about the degree of something, not as a modifier for an adjective like "extravagant".

questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the words/sentence.

A sheath for the blade of a sword.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1' i.e. 'Scabbard'.

Key Points

  • The best substitute for the given words/sentence "A sheath for the blade of a sword" is "Scabbard."
  • Scabbard: A protective sheath or case for the blade of a sword or dagger.(छाल)
  • For example: "He carefully slid the sword back into its scabbard."

Therefore, the correct answer is- 'Scabbard'.

Additional Information

  • Denude: To strip or remove something, particularly in the context of removing covering or protection. (नंगा करना)
    • For example: "The construction workers denuded the building of its old facade."
  • Divulge: To reveal or make known, typically confidential or secret information.( खोलना)
    • For example: "The detective refused to divulge any details of the ongoing investigation."
  • Expose: To reveal or make something visible or known, often referring to exposing to danger or harm.( बेनकाब करना)
    • For example: "The journalist's investigative report exposed corruption within the government."
